Women Who Rewrote Tennis History

100 Years of Sci-Fi 
Science fiction has long been an outlet for human curiosity. Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein (1818) is often credited as the spark that brought modern sci-fi to life. No less important are the works of Jules Verne and H.G. Wells, which formed its backbone. But it wasn’t until 1926, when Hugo Gernsback’s pulp magazine Amazing Stories was first published, that sci-fi became a genre

images.alt: Amazing Stories, April 1926. Pulp magazine cover. Experimenter Publishing Company, New York. Hugo Gernsback, editor. Sto

regions.text:
Visions of tomorrow, printed today
Amazing Stories was the first to exclusively publish sci-fi stories, and it has continued to do so for a century (under various owners). Sci-fi’s top honor, the Hugo Award, is named for Gernsback in recognition of his indelible contributions to the genre.

The future is now
Sci-fi writing has been enriched over the decades by the boundless imagination of such luminaries as Robert A. Heinlein, Isaac Asimov, and Arthur C. Clarke. It has become a staple of film too: One of the biggest movies of 2026 is an adaptation of Andy Weir’s Project Hail Mary. Read about its mind-bending science.
From Amazing Stories, Experimenter Publishing Company, April 1926.
